verdict: Not today. The carcass is in good shape. The cut list, the DXFs and cad.json agree on every panel, cut-out and rebate and on the amplifier's cut-out, so a CNC shop could cut the panels and you could glue up both boxes. The roof cannot be finished as drawn, in either size. The tweeter's flange (73 mm; the bookshelf's 62 mm faceplate) is drawn in a counterbore at the throat with a smaller bore behind it (67 mm; 49 mm), so it cannot be seated 'from behind' as sheet 3 says. The gable's two front dowels stand 5 mm inside the insert's foot, so the insert cannot slide home. The upper two magnets sit on the tweeter's boss, so their partners have no wall to sit in. Many smaller gaps force guesses. No sheet or file shows the screw holes for the drivers, the amplifier plate or the tweeter. The trim rings have no file and no size, and the magnets and pins have no dimensions. The amplifier box and the port are missing from the section, no sheet gives the port's length, and the port STL is 5 mm longer than acoustics.json says. The gland is given in three sizes and two positions. The bookshelf's sheets and folders still include a window brace it no longer has. The drawn cable runs pass through the brace. Every piece of text except the sheet number is under 2.5 mm high.

findings.where: SECTION ON THE AXIS (WITH THE GABLE), the tweeter's flange and the bore behind it: floorstander crop (2100, 270, 2300, 590), bookshelf crop (2250, 330, 2440, 830). The BACK view shows the narrower bore through the boss: floorstander (735, 1355, 1010, 1625).
findings.problem: The tweeter cannot be seated 'from behind' as note 2 says: its flange sits in a counterbore at the throat with a smaller bore behind it, so the 45 mm throat traps it at the front and the bore traps it at the back.
findings.evidence: Sheet 3 labels the 'counterbore ø73.4 x 6.2 for the tweeter's flange', and note 2 says 'Seat the tweeter in the counterbore from behind'. cad.waveguide_insert cuts that counterbore only from y 176 to 182.2. Behind it is a ø67 bore (TWEETER_PART body_d 66 + 1) to y 217, which the 73 mm flange (flange_d 73) cannot pass, and in front the throat is ø45 (r0 22.5). Bookshelf: a ø62.4 x 4.7 counterbore at y 95 to 99.7 behind a ø34 throat, with a ø49 bore (body_d 48 + 1) to y 132 inside a ø60 boss, against a 62 mm faceplate. The floorstander's stl/waveguide-insert-left/-right halves are the only way to get it in, and they leave the tweeter captive. The bookshelf has no halves.
findings.fix: Floorstander: in cad.waveguide_insert, replace the ø67 body bore with the ø73.4 counterbore run from the boss's back (y 217) to the throat plane (y 176), 41 deep, so the flange goes in from behind and seats on the throat ring at y 176. The ø86 boss keeps 6.3 mm walls. Relabel sheet 3: 'counterbore ø73.4 from the back, 41 deep, flange seat at y 176'. Bookshelf: the same ø62.4 bore from y 132 to y 95 needs a ø68.4 boss. Its underside would then be at z 482.8, below the top panel at 484, so the throat must rise to z 519.2 (question 1).

findings.where: Not drawn in any view: the two front dowels under the insert's foot. Sheet-5 item 4 shows the four holes without dimensions; top-panel.dxf DRILL_10_DEEP10 holes at (42, 182) and (312, 182), bookshelf (15.85, 94.82) and (168.15, 94.82).
findings.problem: The gable's two front dowels stand 5 mm inside the insert's foot, so the insert stops 5 mm short of home, and the block's dowel holes break into its pocket.
findings.evidence: cad.dowel_points puts the front pair at (60, 200) and (330, 200): ø10, 10 deep in the top panel and 20 in the block (z 850 to 880). The insert's back face is at y 200, and its outline spans x 53.4 to 336.6 at z 860 and x 58.9 to 331.1 at z 880. Each dowel's y 195 to 205 therefore overlaps the insert's foot by 5 mm over 87 % of its footprint. Bookshelf: dowels at (33.8, 112.8) and (186.2, 112.8), the insert's back at y 113, its outline x 30.4 to 189.6 at z 484: a 5.2 mm overlap over 47 % of the footprint. None of the cad.json checks covers this.
findings.fix: In cad.dowel_points, move the front pair to y 215 for the floorstander: (60, 215) and (330, 215), top-panel DXF holes at (42, 197) and (312, 197). Move them to y 125 for the bookshelf: (33.8, 125) and (186.2, 125), DXF holes at (15.8, 107) and (168.2, 107). That puts them 9.7 and 6.7 mm behind the pocket's back wall. Add a cad.checks entry 'dowels clear of the insert's pocket' with least 3 mm.

findings.where: amp-box-lid.dxf in both sizes. The lid is drawn on no sheet: sheet-4 note 5 (floorstander) and note 4 (bookshelf) are text only.
findings.problem: The lid's gland hole is 25 mm from an unmarked long edge in the DXF but 43 mm from the front edge in the CAD. Drilled 25 mm from the front edge, it lands on the top edge of the box's front panel.
findings.evidence: flats.py writes circle(INNER - 40, 25, gland_d): (314, 25) on a 354 x 108 lid, bookshelf (144, 25) on 184 x 88, with neither edge named. cad.amp_box_panels puts the gland at x 332, y = y0 + 25 = 307, on a lid spanning y 264 to 372, so 43 from its front edge (bookshelf: 157 on 114 to 202, also 43). At 25 from the front edge, the ø25 hole spans y 276.5 to 301.5 over the box front at y 264 to 282: a 5.5 mm overlap. Bookshelf: the ø20 hole spans y 129 to 149 against the front at 114 to 132, a 3 mm overlap. The lock nut sits on the panel in both.
findings.fix: In flats.py use circle(INNER - 40, WALL + 25, AMP_BOX['gland_d']) = (314, 43), bookshelf (144, 43), and add a NOTES text 'FRONT EDGE' along y 0 of amp-box-lid.dxf. Draw the lid in plan on sheet 4 with the hole dimensioned 40 from the right side's inner face and 43 from the lid's front edge.

findings.where: FRONT view rebate notes: floorstander mid (715, 690, 1010, 730) and woofer (830, 1160, 1060, 1195); bookshelf woofer (798, 690, 955, 718).
findings.problem: Each rebate is cut to the flange plus the ring only, with nothing for the flange gasket the research requires, so with a gasket fitted the rings stand proud of the finish.
findings.evidence: params: WOOFER_REBATE depth 8 is 'its flange (about 5) + the 3 mm ring', MID_REBATE 10.5 is 7.5 + 3, and the bookshelf's 9.5 is 6.5 + 3. research/drivers-floorstander.md says: 'Rebate depth = the measured flange thickness + the compressed gasket (about 1-2 mm) + the 3 mm trim ring'. The woofer's box is vented and the mid's chamber is sealed, so both flanges must seal. The SB17NRX2C35-8's flange is 6.5 in drivers-small.md but 'front 10.9' in drivers-floorstander.md (both unconfirmed).
findings.fix: Add a 1.0 mm compressed gasket to each depth: floorstander WOOFER_REBATE depth 9.0 and MID_REBATE 11.5, bookshelf WOOFER_REBATE 10.5. The DXF layers become POCKET_9MM, POCKET_11.5MM and POCKET_10.5MM. Add 'flange on 1.5 mm closed-cell foam, 1.0 compressed' to sheet 1 note 2 and to the BOM.

findings.where: BACK view, the upper two magnets drawn on the boss: floorstander (690, 1395, 740, 1445) and (1000, 1395, 1050, 1445); bookshelf (750, 1370, 810, 1430) and (1070, 1370, 1130, 1430)
findings.problem: The upper two magnets sit on the tweeter's boss. Their holes break into the boss (in the bookshelf, into the tweeter's bore too), and their partner holes fall in the pocket's open boss bore, where there is no wall to hold them.
findings.evidence: cad.insert_fixings puts the upper pair at 60 % of the half-width and 75 % of the height. Floorstander: (155.2, 952.7) and (234.8, 952.7), 43.55 from the axis, so the ø12.2 holes span r 37.45 to 49.65, against the boss at r 43.0 and its bore in the pocket at r 43.3. Bookshelf: (89.7, 532.6) and (130.3, 532.6), 25.59 from the axis, so the ø8.2 holes span r 21.49 to 29.69: wholly inside the boss (r 30) and cutting into the ø49 tweeter bore (r 24.5). The sheet-3 BACK view draws them astride the boss circles. Only the pins are kept clear of the boss.
findings.fix: In cad.insert_fixings, put the upper pair level with the axis, outboard of the boss: floorstander x 195 ± 70 at z 935 (13 mm inside the outline, 20.6 mm clear of the boss bore); bookshelf x 110 ± 40 at z 517 (12.7 mm inside, 5.6 mm clear). Add a cad.checks entry 'magnets and pins clear of the boss bore' with least 3 mm.

findings.where: BACK, the amplifier plate: floorstander (290, 1545, 860, 1765), bookshelf (430, 910, 755, 1740)
findings.problem: Sheet 4 does not say how the amplifier plate is held or sealed: no screw holes, no rebate size as cut, no gasket.

Add 'ten ø3.5 pilot holes, 25 deep, to Hypex's FA253 (FA122) drawing'. Add 'Hypex Fusion Mounting Screws, 10 x 4.3 x 25' and '3 mm closed-cell EPDM tape' to the BOM.

findings.evidence: Sheet 3 labels only 'magnet ø12x4' and 'pin ø6'. cad.insert_fixings puts the magnets at x 195 ± 75.9, z 890.9 and x 195 ± 39.8, z 952.7, and the pins at x 195 ± 84.1, z 915.8. Bookshelf: magnets at x 110 ± 41.4, z 500.2 and x 110 ± 20.3, z 532.6; pins at x 110 ± 48.1, z 510.4. The magnet holes are ø12.2 x 4.3 in the insert and 4.0 deep from the pocket wall. The pin holes are ø6.1 x 5.5 in the insert and 5.2 in the wall. Bookshelf: ø8.2 x 3.3 / 3.0 and ø4.1 x 4.5 / 4.2. A 6.1 hole grips a 6.0 pin in neither part.

Specify the pins as 'pressed into ø5.9 x 5.5 in the insert, a slip fit in ø6.2 x 5.5 in the wall' (bookshelf ø3.9 and ø4.2), and the magnets as 'ø12.2 x 4.3, epoxied, poles marked'.

findings.where: sheet-1 note 2 (2355, 1205, 2805, 1262) and the FRONT view's rings; sheet-5 item 13
findings.problem: The trim rings have no file and no size. The BOM calls them a friction fit, but each sits in a rebate 0.8 mm larger all round, and its flat back rests on the flange where the screw heads stand.
findings.evidence: out*/stl and out*/step hold no ring. components.trim_ring makes the woofer's ring OD 314.0 / ID 284.1, the mid's 165.0 / 136.1 and the bookshelf's 171.0 / 147.0, all 3.0 thick. That is 1.6 under the 315.6 / 166.6 / 172.6 rebates, which is params' '0.8 reveal'. The BOM and params also call the ring 'a friction fit'. The rebate is the flange plus 3, so the ring's back lands on the screw heads, and the research specifies 'stainless button-head screws under the trim rings'.
findings.fix: Export stl/trim-ring-woofer.stl and stl/trim-ring-mid.stl (bookshelf: stl/trim-ring-woofer.stl) at those sizes and list them on sheet 1. Give each ring a groove on its back, 2.0 deep and 10 wide, on the driver's bolt circle for M4 low-head screws (head 1.6 or less). Replace 'friction fit' with 'held by three 5 mm dots of neutral-cure silicone; 0.8 reveal all round'.

findings.where: SECTION A-A, the back wall at z 405 (250, 1240, 285, 1400). Sheet-4 BACK gives only '405'.
findings.problem: No sheet gives the port's length, and the printed tube in the STL is 5 mm longer than acoustics.json's.
findings.evidence: acoustics.json gives tube_length_mm 153.3 'from the flange face to the collar' and total 171.3, and the README says 'port 171 mm'. stl/port-tube-with-flange.stl spans y 236.7 to 395.0, which is 158.3 from the flange's outer face, and 176.3 with the collar (to y 218.7), because cad.port_parts runs the bore from +5 (the flange face) to -153.3. The BOM says 'Print 10 mm long', which means longer. No sheet gives the ø92 bore, the ø100 OD in the ø100.5 hole, the ø112 x 5 flange, or how the flange is fixed.
findings.fix: In cad.port_parts, run the bore from axial 0 to -(L - T) so the tube is 153.3 from the flange face and 171.3 to the flare's lip. Draw the port in section A-A with 153.3 (flange face to the tube's end), 18 (collar) and 171.3 overall, the ø92 bore, the ø100 OD in the ø100.5 hole, and the ø112 x 5 flange 'glued to the finish'. In the BOM: 'print 10 mm longer (163.3), measure the impedance dip, trim to 32 Hz'.

findings.where: 'Runs, connectors and seals': floorstander note 5 (1085, 1752, 1560, 1800), bookshelf note 4 (1085, 1642, 1550, 1660)
findings.problem: Sheet 4 gives the lid's gland as 20 mm PG11 (floorstander) and 16 mm (bookshelf), against M25 and M20 everywhere else.
findings.evidence: params AMP_BOX gland_d 25.0 is 'an M25 with a three-hole seal' (bookshelf 20.0, 'an M20 with a two-hole seal'). amp-box-lid.dxf cuts ø25.0 (bookshelf ø20.0), and the BOM says 'M25 three-hole (floorstander), M20 two-hole (bookshelf)'. sheets.py hard-codes '20 mm gland (PG11)' and '16 mm gland', the values before the 2026-10-08 change. PG11 is an 18.6 mm thread. The lid is 18 thick, more than a standard gland's 8 to 10 mm thread.
findings.fix: Build the note from AMP_BOX: 'an M25 x 1.5 long-thread (15 mm) gland with a three-hole seal, in a ø25.5 hole, its lock nut in a ø40 x 8 counterbore under the lid' (bookshelf: M20 x 1.5, two-hole seal, ø20.5 hole, ø32 x 8 counterbore). Cut the DXF holes at ø25.5 and ø20.5.

findings.where: 'Fitting the tweeter and the insert' note 4 (1805, 1655, 2495, 1718); the section's bay, channel and grommet (1985, 380, 2125, 815)

At z 927 the roof's surface is at y 87. With the 120 mm tweeter lead, the insert comes out only about 127 mm, with its foot still in the pocket. Bookshelf: 33 in the channel and 67 left, so the socket reaches y 75, 39 behind the roof at y 36. That works.
findings.fix: Change sheet 3 note 4 for the floorstander to 'The cabinet's lead ends in the socket 250 mm above the grommet' (67 in the channel, 167 from the bay floor to 20 mm proud of the roof at z 927, 16 of slack). Keep 100 mm for the bookshelf.

findings.where: Every title block (2043, 2051, 3221, 2254)
findings.problem: No sheet gives a general tolerance, or the fits for the printed parts, the CNC pockets and the holes.

questions.question: Bookshelf tweeter: the README puts 'its 62 mm faceplate on the insert's back', but the CAD seats it in a counterbore at the throat, 18 mm in front of the insert's back (y 113), with 1.8 mm of insert under it. To let it in from behind, the boss must grow from ø60 to about ø68.4, which needs the throat raised from z 517 to about 519.2 (the study simulated 514). Should it be raised, or should the insert be printed in two halves around the tweeter, giving up servicing it?
questions.why: The waveguide's position came from the simulation, so only you can move it 2 mm or accept a captive tweeter.

questions.question: TW29DN-B fixing: SB's faceplate screws thread into the motor, and the research suggests screwing a throat ring to the motor from the front, as SB's adapter does. Sheet 3 instead drives M3 screws from behind into heat-set inserts in the insert, which needs the motor's tapped holes opened to clearance. Which way is intended?
questions.why: It decides whether the insert gets clearance holes, with screw heads inside the throat, or heat-set inserts in the flange's seat; the research gives the screws as 'likely M3 or M4; count n/f'.

questions.question: TW29DN-B counterbore: the research gives the bare motor as 71 to 74 mm across and its pocket as about 75 mm; the CAD's counterbore is 73.4 (flange_d 73 + 0.4). Keep 73.4 until one is measured, or cut 75?
questions.why: A 74 mm motor will not enter a 73.4 counterbore, and the insert is a print, so getting it wrong costs a reprint.

questions.question: Bookshelf gable: the boss's bore leaves 2.7 mm of birch above the block's base (bore ø60.6 at z 517, base at 484), and 3.0 mm between the bore and the cable channel (y 132 to 135). Will a laminated or printed gable hold those webs, or should the channel move back?
questions.why: Both webs sit in the first 18 mm birch layer and would break out when it is milled.

questions.question: Text height: at 2.5 mm caps (10 pt), the notes will not fit on sheets 1 to 4 as laid out. Do you accept a sixth sheet for the panel details (d20) and a seventh for the notes?
questions.why: The legibility rule and the current sheet layout cannot both hold.

questions.question: SB17NRX2C35-8 flange: drivers-small.md gives 6.5 mm (the rebate's 9.5 is 6.5 + 3), but drivers-floorstander.md gives a 'front' of 10.9. Which is right?
questions.why: At 10.9, the flush rebate would be 14.9 to 15.9 deep in the 18 mm baffle, leaving 2 to 3 mm of wood for the screws.
